profilePeriod: Federal political career, particularly 2018–2022 premiership, checked against public statements through 2026-09-08
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

sources.title: Nikkei Asia Forum: economic security
sources.evidence: Defends Quad and trusted supply chains, state support and price floors for critical minerals; rejects need to onshore every stage. Supports gas investment and federal control of foreign relations.

sources.title: GST reforms were not a zero-sum game
sources.evidence: Defends WA retaining benefits of resource development while retaining reasonable fiscal equalisation and extra support for the Northern Territory.

sources.title: National Cabinet press conference
sources.evidence: Calls states and territories sovereign and autonomous decision-makers while seeking coordinated national pandemic response.

sources.title: Bell Inquiry report
sources.evidence: Secret appointment to five departments prevented parliamentary accountability; inquiry identifies undermining of responsible government. This is a serious practice-versus-democratic-principle tension.

sources.title: Scott Morrison concedes defeat
sources.evidence: Concedes federal election defeat, evidencing acceptance of electoral alternation.

sources.title: Interview on encryption legislation
sources.evidence: Defends police access to encrypted communications to combat terrorism, organised crime and child exploitation.

sources.title: Interview on Australian gun laws
sources.evidence: Calls restrictive gun laws a proud Liberal-National achievement that kept Australia safe; rejects weakening them.

sources.title: Vaccination interview
sources.evidence: Clarifies that vaccination will not be compulsory for all; aims for high voluntary uptake. Later targeted occupational mandates cannot imply endorsement of universal forced vaccination.

sources.title: Launch of death-penalty abolition strategy
sources.evidence: Morrison government foreign minister launches whole-of-government opposition to capital punishment, citing irreversible error, rehabilitation and human dignity.

sources.title: Migration and settlement speech
sources.evidence: Praises multicultural migration and refugee settlement, English learning and national cohesion; defends capped skills-based migration and strong border protection.

sources.title: Anti-Semitism conference speech
sources.evidence: Continues praising cultural diversity while condemning Islamist and far-right antisemitism; argues constructive religion strengthens liberal society. His allegations about particular events are his stated interpretation, not independent findings.

sources.title: AUKUS address
sources.evidence: Supports nuclear-powered submarines and close US/UK alliance; expressly rejects acquiring nuclear weapons or establishing civilian nuclear capability as part of that agreement.

sources.title: Support for US strikes on Iran
sources.evidence: Explicitly supports targeted US strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities as deterrence after failed diplomacy; advocates AUKUS and allied solidarity, but describes objective as stopping weapons capability rather than regime change.

sources.title: JobKeeper update
sources.evidence: Government funded emergency private-sector wage subsidies; initial fiscal estimate was revised, so announced initial cost must not be treated as realised spending.

sources.title: Guaranteeing Medicare overview
sources.evidence: Morrison government budget increased Medicare funding and described affordable universal healthcare as a policy pillar.

sources.title: Business address on climate and enterprise
sources.evidence: Champions private enterprise and technology over carbon taxes/regulation; endorses net zero by 2050 and state-enabled technology investment rather than consumption contraction.

sources.title: G20 press conference on trade
sources.evidence: Champions free and open trade and reform of rules-based multilateral trading system.

sources.title: Scott Morrison conservative on abortion
sources.evidence: States personal conservative abortion views but leaves NSW legislation to state MPs and does not seek a federal intervention.

sources.title: ABC 7.30 campaign interview
sources.evidence: Describes Christian faith in terms of love and service, supports NDIS and mental-health spending; prioritises Australian interests in external decisions.

sources.title: Same-sex marriage final vote
sources.evidence: Morrison abstained from the final marriage-equality vote; distinguish personal opposition from a recorded final parliamentary no vote.

sources.title: Stem-cell therapies mission
sources.evidence: Government funded stem-cell research for chronic and inherited disease. This supports therapeutic biotechnology, not unrestricted enhancement of embryos.

sources.title: Australia first mission to Moon
sources.evidence: Government announced Australian lunar mission, supporting a practical pro-space industrial outlook.

sources.title: Author book page
sources.evidence: Scott Morrison authored Plans for Your Good, mixing Christian testimony with an account of national leadership, global crises and secularisation; site stresses pastoral encouragement.

sources.title: Publishers Weekly review: Plans for Your Good
sources.evidence: Identifies Scott Morrison as author, Thomas Nelson publisher and May publication; verifies substantive discussions of government mental-health policy, Afghanistan withdrawal, China and nuclear submarines alongside personal faith.

sources.title: English-language edition sold in Portugal
sources.evidence: Lists original title and English language. Dedicated Brazilian-title searches did not verify a Brazilian Portuguese translation.

sources.title: Religious discrimination legislation explained
sources.evidence: Explains religious-expression protections and contested LGBT-student safeguards; shows conservative faith policy within legislation and pluralist institutions, not formal theocracy.

sources.title: Latest speeches index
sources.evidence: Current-date dedicated search and official speech index returned September 2026 economic-security remarks as newest indexed speech; no claim of exhaustive coverage of unindexed remarks.

facts: States retain autonomous powers within coordinated National Cabinet.
GST reform keeps fiscal equalisation but rewards state resource development.
Foreign policy remains a Commonwealth prerogative.
estrutura.tension: Federalism with national standards and fiscal transfers; neither secessionism nor unitary government.

facts: Accepted defeat in the 2022 election.
Secret ministry appointments impaired parliamentary accountability.
representacao.tension: Democratic party government and electoral consent coexist with unusually secretive executive practice; neither direct-democracy radical nor autocrat.

facts: Backed access to encrypted communications and strong gun controls.
Government opposes death penalty; he rejected universal compulsory vaccination.
poder.tension: Strong policing is limited by due process and some personal liberties; do not conflate security policy with support for executions.

facts: Celebrates multicultural migration, English learning and skills selection.
Maintains capped migration and strict border control.
imigracao.tension: Civic integration and regulated admission coexist with cultural pluralism; border enforcement is not racial homogenisation.

facts: Established AUKUS nuclear-powered submarine partnership.
Endorsed US Iran strikes in 2025 as necessary deterrence after diplomacy.
diplomacia.tension: Military deterrence and selected force, but no Australian nuclear weapons or unconditional war policy.

facts: Strong US/UK security alliances and Quad engagement.
Endorses strategic pressure and targeted allied intervention.
intervencao.tension: National interest through alliances and international rules; rejects isolationism without claiming imperial conquest.

facts: Supports private enterprise as engine of growth.
Retains Medicare and emergency employer wage support.
economia.tension: Private ownership with funded public services and safety nets, not either full nationalisation or privatisation of every state function.

facts: Favours less regulatory/tax burden on enterprise.
Adopted emergency spending and endorses strategic industrial support including price floors.
controle.tension: Market allocation alongside countercyclical and security-driven interventions; not comprehensive central planning.

facts: Champions free trade and multilateral trading rules.
Supports trusted allied supply chains without requiring everything produced domestically.
comercio.tension: Economic-security exceptions without blanket tariffs or autarky.

facts: Christian faith explicitly guides service and moral outlook.
Promotes religious expression protections and constructive public religion.
religiao.tension: Personal and public faith within pluralist constitutional government, not compulsory religious identity.

facts: Personally conservative on abortion and traditional marriage.
Abstained from final marriage bill vote and leaves state abortion legislation to state process.
moral.tension: Social conservatism bounded by tolerance, democratic settlement and equal citizenship; specific answers beyond record are cautious inference.

facts: Advocates technology-led climate policy, lunar capability and therapeutic stem-cell research.
Sustains gas and mining industries.
tecnologia.tension: Industrial technophilia with ethical caution on embryo enhancement; no evidence for limitless transhumanism.

uncertainties: No prior answer archive, stored vector, similarity review or score report consulted.
Later statements included under existing career-wide period; profilePeriod text preserved verbatim with separate current verification date.

Brazil-specific hypotheticals interpreted as comparable Australian policy questions; community-rule and land-redistribution questions do not imply literal Australian endorsement of Brazilian institutions.

Some micro-issues, including brain implants, cultured meat, municipal constitutions and crypto currency competition lack a direct personal quotation. Answers are bounded inferences from documented policy, never neutrals solely for missing evidence.
Official self-descriptions establish stated positions; independent ABC, SBS/AAP and Bell inquiry evidence supplies counterweight.
Latest indexed evidence does not prove absence of every later statement.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored mixed spiritual and political memoir. No Brazilian translation verified; retain original title. Existing books.json had no entry.
